description: Chilaquiles Red Salsa is a beloved Mexican breakfast, transforming simple tortillas into a comforting and flavorful dish. Crispy fried tortilla pieces are simmered in a vibrant, spicy red salsa until just tender, then topped generously with crema, queso fresco, and fresh onion. It's a hearty and satisfying way to start any day, bursting with authentic Mexican flavors.

cut into quarters or strips, day-old preferred

instructions.title: Prepare the Chiles and Tomatoes
instructions.text: Place the dried guajillo and arbol chiles, halved Roma tomatoes, garlic cloves, and a quarter of the white onion in a saucepan. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes until the chiles are softened and the tomatoes are tender. Drain, reserving some of the cooking liquid.

instructions.title: Blend the Red Salsa
instructions.text: Transfer the softened chiles, tomatoes, garlic, and onion to a blender. Add 1 cup of chicken broth and blend until completely smooth. If the mixture is too thick, add a little more of the reserved chile cooking liquid or chicken broth until you reach a pourable consistency. Season with salt.

instructions.title: Fry the Tortilla Chips
instructions.text: Heat about 1 inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Once hot, fry the corn tortilla pieces in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per batch. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil. Season lightly with salt.

instructions.title: Simmer the Red Salsa
instructions.text: In a clean large skillet or Dutch oven, heat 3 tablespoons of vegetable oil over medium heat. Pour the blended red salsa through a fine-mesh sieve into the hot oil, pressing on the solids to extract all liquid. Discard the solids. Bring the salsa to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, allowing it to thicken slightly and deepen in flavor. Add the remaining 2 cups of chicken broth and adjust seasoning if needed.

instructions.title: Combine Chips and Salsa
instructions.text: Just before serving, add the fried tortilla chips to the simmering red salsa. Gently toss to coat the chips evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the chips are just softened but still have a slight bite. Do not overcook, or they will become soggy.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Immediately transfer the chilaquiles to individual plates. Garnish generously with a drizzle of Mexican crema, crumbled queso fresco, chopped fresh cilantro, and finely diced white onion. For a heartier meal, top each serving with a freshly fried egg. Serve hot and enjoy this authentic Mexican breakfast!

tips: For truly authentic flavor, always use dried chiles instead of chili powder. Toasting them lightly before simmering can enhance their aroma.
If you dont have fresh tortillas to fry, good quality store-bought tortilla chips can be used as a shortcut, but ensure they are plain and unsalted.
Chilaquiles are best served immediately after combining the chips and salsa to prevent them from becoming too soggy. Prepare all toppings in advance.
